text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--Trade Minister Jan Troejborg does not support a ministry proposal to relax supervision of smaller businesses, so that they must only have accounts audited every three or four years.
--Carlsberg leads the Taiwanese beer market after forming an alliance with the country's biggest distributor.
--Foreign companies, particularly Americans, will buy up Danish data firms at an increasing rate.
--A.P.Moeller's Maersk Oil has sold two drill rigs for a total of 1.5 billion crowns.
--Economy Minister Marianne Jelved says that she no longer opposes an EU-wide minimum rate of corporation tax.
--Airline groupings such as the Star Alliance, of which SAS is a member, have led to reduced competition and higher prices on some routes.
--The number of cases of improper securities trading is rising. Last year the financial supervisory authority investigated more cases than in the preceding seven years combined.
